statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail holds at 20%, the floor of the watch band, because the improvement from the previous hour has continued and broadened: the Nasdaq-100 cash index is 30,522.06, now +0.37% on the day and about 247 points above the 30,274.65 session low it rejected, VIX has decayed to 16.81 from a 17.59 session high, and the 10-year Treasury yield is 5.22% after peaking at 5.34%, its highest since 2002, with the 2-year 13 basis points lower at 4.78%. Stress eases to 74% because the rates and energy backdrop remains difficult even as the intraday amplifiers decay.
recommendation: Tail remains at 20%, the lower edge of the watch band, and the mapped policy state is unchanged at WATCH. The decisive observation is that the session low has now been fully retraced rather than merely held: an hour ago price sat about 90 points above the rejected low with the index still negative on the day, and it is now positive and in the upper half of its range while volatility, yields and crude all stay below their session extremes. That is the orderly price discovery and cross-asset stabilisation this contract treats as grounds for Tail to remain at the band floor, and no observed structure supports a move toward the block threshold. The environment nonetheless stays difficult, so Stress remains high at 74%: the cash range spans 302 points, the 10-year sits at 5.22% after the biggest quarterly yield rise this century, and Brent holds above $100. The narrow danger window covers the final US cash hour from 19:00Z to 20:00Z, where late-session continuation or reversal is the next genuine checkpoint. Tail is described here as a risk score only, with no position, sizing or account-specific guidance attached.
headline: Tail holds at the 20% watch floor as the index fully retraces its session low; yields and volatility ease further and Stress slips to 74%
body: The Nasdaq-100 picture has improved again, and the improvement is now broad rather than partial. At the 17:30Z cutoff the cash index is 30,522.06 on Yahoo Finance and 30,525.79 on Investing.com, up 0.37-0.39% against a 30,408.50 previous close, which means the morning fade has been fully retraced and the index is positive on the day. Price sits roughly 247 points above the 30,274.65 session low it rejected and about 51 points below the 30,576.44 high, in the upper half of a 302-point cash range rather than pinned at an extreme. NQ futures are 30,672.00, down 0.09% against a 30,698.75 previous close and about 143 points above their 30,529.25 session low, so the continuous reference is close to flat while cash is modestly higher - a divergence that argues for a mixed dominant mode rather than a directional one. Every amplifier that drove the morning fade has continued to decay. VIX is 16.81, up 2.87% on the day but clearly below the 17.59 session high and above the 16.21 low, so volatility is decaying into the afternoon rather than expanding. The rates channel has eased further: the 10-year Treasury yield is 5.22%, roughly seven basis points lower on the day and twelve below the 5.34% intraday peak that was its highest since 2002, with the 2-year at 4.78% after a 13 basis point decline and the 30-year at 5.59%. Reuters reporting carried by Yahoo Finance frames that peak within a global bond rout in which the 10-year posted its biggest quarterly yield rise this century, French 10-year costs approached 5% and the UK 30-year exceeded 6%; the retreat from 5.34% to the mid-5.2s is the relief that matters for this hour. Energy is unchanged to marginally softer against the previous hour, with WTI at $91.72, up 1.44%, and Brent at $100.84, up 2.87%. Under this contract the combination of a rejected session low fully retraced, volatility decaying, and both yields and crude off their extremes is the orderly, mean-reverting price discovery that permits Tail to stay at the watch floor rather than rebuild. The macro inputs behind the session are unchanged and independently verified. The ISM Manufacturing PMI released at 14:00Z registered 54.5 against 54.6 in August, a ninth consecutive month of expansion, with New Orders 55.3, Production 56.7 and Employment 52.7. The market-relevant component remains Prices at 77.9, up 6.8 points from 71.1, with respondents citing pricing volatility, tariffs, geopolitical tension and extended lead times; that is the standing reason the rates channel stays sensitive even on a day when it fades. Initial jobless claims at 197,000 marked a fourth consecutive weekly decline. Energy remains a standing amplifier rather than a fresh shock: Brent moved above $100 after Chinese refiners suspended October fuel exports outside Hong Kong and Macau, with PetroChina cancelling gasoline and jet-fuel cargoes and domestic inventories reported near seven-year lows, in a market already constrained by the US-Iran conflict and the war in Ukraine. Strait of Hormuz transits remain near 3% of pre-war levels, and tanker strikes continued on 30 September and 1 October, but that is a persistent background condition rather than new escalation today, so it informs Stress and not Tail. At the single-name level the tape remains mixed rather than one-way, which reduces directional conviction: Micron was roughly flat despite a record fiscal fourth quarter of $54.23 billion in revenue and fiscal-Q1 guidance of about $61.5 billion, while Amazon, AMD and Intel were lower as the AI trade cooled and energy outperformed. The September employment report at 12:30Z on 2 October, confirmed against the BLS release schedule, is the next scheduled catalyst. No outcome for it is assumed anywhere in this assessment; under this contract its proximity lifts conditional Stress into the extreme band around the release while conditional Tail stays capped one point below the block threshold. Taken together: Tail 20%, unchanged at the floor of the watch band; Stress 74%, two points lower but still high on a wide intraday range and a rates channel at 24-year highs; Confidence 88% on fresh levels cross-checked across two independent sources for the index, plus verified futures, 2-year, 10-year and 30-year yields, volatility, crude and a verified release calendar. Dominant mode stays mixed. The shared Finviz context file carried a 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z collection time, roughly 42 hours old, with a partial collection status, so it was treated as stale and unhealthy under the inherited contract and contributed nothing here; all evidence above came from independent primary-source research.

lookbackSummary: Across the preceding 24 hours Claude published an unbroken watch-band regime with a single orange hour. Tail ran between 20% and 25%, touching the 25% block threshold once in the 06:00Z hour on a trend-up reading before easing back when that structure failed to persist, then reaching 24% in the 14:00Z hour as the US cash open reversed the overnight rally. Stress climbed from 72% to a window high of 78% in the 14:00Z and 15:00Z hours before easing to 76%, and Confidence held at 87-89% throughout. Dominant mode was mixed in 22 of the 24 hours, with trend-up only in the 05:00Z and 06:00Z hours. The window describes a market absorbing a high-rates, high-energy-price environment through two-way ranges rather than a persistent one-way path, which is why the published action stayed at WATCH for 23 of the 24 hours.
outlookSummary: The near path turns on whether the fully retraced 30,274.65 cash low keeps holding while volatility and yields continue to decay. Conditional Tail holds 20% for the current and next hour while the 30,408.50 previous close and the 30,576.44 high bracket price, ticks to 21% for the 19:00Z final cash hour on late-session continuation or reversal risk, then returns to 20% at the close and decays to 18-19% across the post-close and Asian hours as liquidity thins and the assumed regime becomes quiet consolidation. From the 05:00Z European handover the conditional path rebuilds to 20-22% on the payrolls countdown, and conditional Stress moves into the extreme band at 82-83% around the 12:30Z September employment report while conditional Tail is capped at 24%, one point below the block threshold, because no release outcome is assumed and a pathological path would require observed repeated extension after a failed retracement. The path then eases to 22-23% through the 2 October US open and midday.
